profile.headline: Contract Software Developer at Intel Corporation
profile.summary:
A dynamic multi-talented engineer looking for an entry to mid-level engineering position, part time ok.

Specialties: c, c++,  client/server,  computer hardware, digital design,  doors,  electrical engineering,  embedded c, graphical user interface, image processing, java, macintosh os,  maple,  matlab, c #, windows, multimeter, oscilloscope, perl, real time, systems engineering,  tcp/ip,  teaching,  usb,  vba,  vhdl, visual basic.

positions.title: Contract Software Developer
positions.description: Worked on bug fixes for the energy measurement system firmware.  Did bug fixes and added features to the data collection and data analysis tools in C#.  Developed several command line tools in C# to expedite data analysis.

positions.title: Contract embedded developer
positions.description:
Worked on an SPI Ethernet controller.
Developed ZigBee library for use in a fob, used Ember stack and IAR Workbench.

positions.title: Contract iOS developer
positions.description:
Assisted in the design of identity management application and libraries for iOS and Android devices.  Did development for iOS using Web Kit, APNS push notifications, Javascript and HTML 5.  Used RSA and Arcot One Time Password libraries.  Also did development on the Motorola Atrix to use the on board fingerprint sensor as an authentication factor.

Some short contracts doing iOS bug fixes and GUI enhancements for CompanionLink Software.

positions.title: Hardware/Software Engineer
positions.description:
I was primarily responsible for maintaining the firmware and hardware for Cryptolex's biometric platform.  I made changes to the firmware and tested their board to make sure it was working and did repairs in case the hardware wasn't working by replacing components and reflashing the firmware.
August 2007 – May 2009

I ported their cryptography library from C to C#, then to Objective C, and finally to Java for use on the Blackberry platform.  Maintained library for use in embedded systems.
August 2007 - August 2009.

I wrote a Windows application to run their cryptography library in C#.  It communicated with UPEK and Authentec USB fingerprint sensors.
August 2007 – May 2009.

Ported old Java networking applet to a newer version of Java.  Also tested Microsoft's WPF technologies to assess its usefulness for future GUI development.
January 2008 - February 2008.

Performed research and development on Hidden Markov Models to investigate voice authentication techniques.  Software was written in C.  Ran simulations in Matlab.
February 2008 - December 2008.

Worked with Spanish voice biometric company Agnitio to integrate their Kivox authenticator with the Windows application.  The application was written in Visual C++.  Used DirectX 9 to record audio.
August 2008 - December 2008.

iPhone lead for identity management and payment system called Mobio.  Mobio was meant to generate a one time code to allow the user to log on to sites using OpenID or enter a secure area.  Mobio could also generate a one time credit card value after scanning a QR code in real time using the iPhone's camera.  This was done so the user could securely shop online and as a workaround for the lack of Near Field Communication (NFC) readers in brick and mortar retail shops at the time.  The application also used the iPhone's Keychain Access and encryption libraries.  Used Jira for project tracking.
http://www.mobioid.com
August 2008 - September 2009.

positions.title: Hardware/Software Engineer
positions.description:
Wrote an application for Palm OS and Windows in C and J2ME to test Bluetooth functionality.  Performed hardware testing and fixes on hand held security devices running ARM 6.  Flashed new devices.  Used JTAG and microcontroller programmers.

Did contract work for a security company to create a solution that used their algorithm with the Biometric Solution fingerprint sensor on a ZigBee capable Microchip PIC Microcontroller.  Tested and wired the Microchip ZigBee development kit to our board.  I worked on the firmware for our board to integrate the cryptography algorithm and programmed in Assembly to enable ZigBee wireless functionality.

Designed real time image processing algorithm to stitch incoming fingerprint frames in embedded C for new lower cost biometric sensor running on Atmel ARM 9.  Also designed an image filter to remove streaks created by the image stitching which resulted in a %30 improvement in performance.  I used Matlab in the design of the image filter. 

Helped to add USB functionality to hardware development kit firmware under eCOS using embedded C.  Also soldered RS232 hardware to our board for testing serial communications as the senior hardware designer forgot to include it.  We had two versions of the dev kit, one running ARM 7 and one running ARM 9.

Developed Windows Plug and Play USB driver to communicate with hardware development kit using KMDF and then later upgraded to WDF.  Also did development on OSX version of the driver.

Developed an application for Windows in C# to view proprietary images in Windows obtained from the hardware development kit.  Later enhanced the application to be able to download images directly from the hardware development kit using either RS232 (serial communications) or USB.  Also enhanced application to be able to compare multiple fingerprints and plot Relative Operating Characteristics curve to show performance of matching algorithm.

positions.title: Electrical Engineering Co-op
positions.description:
Was responsible for analyzing data for aircraft landing prediction algorithm.  Wrote PERL script to extract data for analysis on Solaris.  Used Matlab to do the analysis to determine how well the algorithm was performing and to generate the reports.  This was an FAA regulated environment.
June 2004 - December 2004.

positions.title: Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Lab teaching assistant for junior Electrical Engineering course in analog design.  Duties included helping students with class material, helping students debug circuits, grading lab reports, teaching them how to use LabView, debug SPICE models, and setting up equipment such as digital multi-meters and oscilloscopes.
August 2002 - December 2002.

Lab teaching assistant for freshman Electrical Engineering course in digital design.  Duties included helping students with class material, helping students debug circuits, grading lab reports, debug LogicWorks models, and setting up equipment.
August 2001 - May 2002.

positions.title: Engineer II
positions.description:
Co-wrote the training manual used for integrating and testing the communication equipment in the Greek Patriot program.  The equipment was also extensively tested in a regulated environment before delivery to the customer.  I had to repair the cables and attenuators.  I had to build a power supply filter for a set of radios with noisy power supplies.  Also involved in training military personnel in the use and maintenance of equipment. 
November 2000 - July 2001.
 
Performed study to compare wireless technologies and determine which would be best for on field military personnel. 
May 2000 - November 2000.

positions.title: Engineer II
positions.description:
Wrote test plan and test procedure for testing the power converters in the Iridium system. 
October 1999 - November 1999. 

Created a Matlab tool to analyze the packet flow of the Iridium system. Matlab GUI API was used to design the application. 
June 1999 - September 1999. 

System architect of the computer interface of the fast packet switch for the Teledesic low-Earth-orbit broadband network. Wrote requirements for how the switch would talk to the main computers. Also wrote the design and requirements documents for various ASICs. Learned about Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) and Ethernet protocols.  I also ran simulations in Matlab to analyze the power distribution under various weather conditions.
March 1998 - May 1999.

positions.title: Engineering Student Trainee
positions.description: Was responsible for recording data during structural tests performed on International Space Station components.  Helped to attach thermistors on equipment to measure heat changes during structural tests, I also repaired bad cables and boards on the data acquisition equipment.  All work had to adhere to NASA aerospace standards and certification was required.
